_doc: WS-0.2 (AUR-ROADMAP-001) — Cato Parity Principle golden vectors. Each vector defines identical inputs for the Node decision core (cato-mcp/gate_core.js) and the Python twin (aureon/mcp/cato_client.py::atomic_settlement_gate). Expected values encode Cato v0.2.2 doctrine: ESCALATE if OFR > 1.0; HOLD if OFR > 0.5 OR gas > 50 gwei OR |SOFR delta| > 10 bps; PROCEED otherwise. Thresholds are strict inequalities — boundary-equal vectors must NOT trip. Editing expectations here is a doctrine event, not a test fix.

vectors._note: IEEE-754: 6.00-5.90 = 9.999999... bps (<10, no trip). A nominal 10.0 bps delta like 5.40-5.30 evaluates to 10.000000000000009 and TRIPS the strict > check identically in Node and Python — the boundary is float-sensitive by construction. Both implementations agree bit-for-bit either way; harness run 2026-07-04 confirmed.

2026-08-21 audit finding: a missing/malformed OFR reading (NaN in production, via parseFloat('.') on a FRED missing-observation marker) must never fall through to PROCEED. null here stands in for 'not a usable number' — isUsableStressReading/_is_usable_stress_reading treat null, NaN, and +/-Infinity identically.

chain_state._doc: Probe state that demonstrated the divergence on 13 Sep 2026: both XRPL and Solana are under the $0.01 ultra-low-fee threshold, so v0.3.0 doctrine picks xrpl.

known_failing.reason: The Node picker prefers XRPL when its fee is under $0.01 (v0.3.0 doctrine). The Python twin has no xrpl branch and resolves solana. This vector documents the gap; it is not to be fixed by editing expectations. Remove this marker in the changeset that lands the PARITY_XRPL.md mirror in aureon/mcp/cato_client.py.

chain_state._doc: Shared chain_state for recommended_chain parity (PROCEED vectors only). Solana fee below $0.01 so the cheapest-wins picker resolves 'solana' on both sides.
